causes.what: The dist-sw-01 uplink went down for about 2 minutes from 17:34 to 17:36 and then recovered. During the outage the web tier (web-01 to web-04) lost connectivity and lb-01 had fewer than 2 healthy backends. All four app servers then took a sudden backlog of about 1400 jobs that is still draining slowly, which explains the current slow HTTP and app responses.

ruled_out: db-01 or db-02 fault: cpu 24%, io wait 4%, slow queries 2.8/s, replication lag 1.3s, app db errors 0, all within the normal range
app-tier code or deploy: app.version stays at 412
dist-sw-02 and core-rtr-01 currently: no loss, links up
an ongoing network fault: ping loss and the link-down alert have all resolved
evidence: 17:34:09 lb-01 had fewer than 2 healthy backends. 17:34:39 core-rtr-01 reported link down to dist-sw-01. Ping loss on dist-sw-01, hv-02 and web-01 to web-04 ran from 17:34 to 17:36. All of these resolved by 17:36:44.

app.queue.depth was normal (20 to 60) until 17:34:54. It stepped to about 1394 at 17:35:54 on app-01, and to about 1380 on app-03 at 17:36:15. It is draining only about 43 per minute, so it is still about 1265 at 17:39.
Slow-response and job-queue alerts fired from 17:36:46 on all 4 app and all 4 web hosts after the link recovered. web-01 http.resp.ms is 2468 and app-01 app.resp.ms is 1802.
db-01 db.conn.count rose from about 65 to 160 only at 17:39, a consequence of the backlog rather than a cause. db-01 cpu, io wait and slow-query rate stayed flat throughout.

Only the dist-sw-01 side showed a link event. dist-sw-02 (app and db tier) had no link event, so the app-tier backlog follows from the web-tier outage and retries. The monitoring data does not show why the link dropped (dist-sw-01 if.errors.rate stayed at 0.2 to 0.8 and was flat).
